items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Roach opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Roach provided Council with moments of reflection.

items.title: June is Indigenous History Month -- an opportunity for the everyone to
notes: learn about and the unique heritage, history and experiences of First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples across Turtle Island and who call this area home locally.

It's a time to honour stories, achievements and the strength of Indigenous Peoples It is also a time to change perspectives and build better relationships by demonstrating follow through on the recommendations in the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls Report, and the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s 94 Calls to Action.
National Indigenous Peoples Day is recognized June 21, a day with significant symbolism as the summer solstice.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: The month of June is a time to recognize and celebrate Two Spirit,
notes: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer, or 2SLGBTQ+, communities. Pride is celebrated in June to mark the first large-scale protests for 2SLGBTQ+ rights took place, most notably the Stonewall riots in 1969.
The rainbow is an important symbol of diversity, support and welcome.
The many rainbows throughout our community serve as a reminder that while there is a lot to celebrate, there is still more work to do.
Happy Pride!

items.title: Wampum Belt Presentation
notes: Sohuwesyoklati (Brian Hill) offered his thanks to Council and the City and introduced Martin Powless, Knowledge Keeper and Wampum Belt Maker, and Rita VanEvery.

In the spirit of Reconciliation, Relationship Building and Indigenous History Month, the City of Waterloo commissioned three replica Wampum belts. Kahlunyunti (Martin Powless) of Oneida Nation of the Thames, the artist who recreated the belts, presented the belts to Council and provided some teaching on their history.

The three belts are the Hiawatha Wampum, the Two-Row Wampum and the Dish with One Spoon Wampum. These belts are a physical representation of the oral history of treaties and settlement of the area around the Great Lakes Region extending along a portion of the St. Lawrence River, which we all call home. These are significant representations of our colonial history and are still seen to this day as a reminder to all of us of the responsibilities we hold as treaty people.

As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Hanmer offered some shoutouts, specifically to Caitlin Kraemer for winning Athlete of the Year and to the Waterloo Minor Hockey Association for being recognized by the Kitchener Sports Association as the Organization of the Year with an Award of Excellence. She also offered congratulations to Cathy Brothers from Capacity Canada who was recognized as Citizen of the Year.

Councillor Vasic mentioned staff and residents have been working together to organize a community garden at Dunvegan Park and it got put up this past weekend. She offered her thanks to all the volunteers.

Councillor Wright gave a shoutout to staff for their support in the launch of Pride Month, with numerous teams working with the BIA, as well as the launch of the Square. It was deeply appreciated and the events were lively and welcoming.

Councillor Bodaly mentioned that the University of Waterloo hosted a conference last week on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals that Mayor McCabe spoke at. He also acknowledged some of the Pride events that happened recently, such as Tri-Pride this past weekend, and the International Day Against Homophobia, Biphobia and Transphobia on May 17th. He and Councillor Roe attended an event in Kitchener that was a good reminder that while Pride is a celebration for many, it is also a protest and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community are still fighting for rights.
